### Problem: Corporate Flight Bookings {#sec-pref-p3-a}

::: {.p-statement}
There are $n$ flights numbered $1 \dots n$ ($1 \le n \le 2\cdot10^4$) and a list of bookings ($\le 2\cdot10^4$ entries). Each booking is $[first, last, seats]$ with $1 \le first \le last \le n$ and $1 \le seats \le 10^4$, meaning *every* flight from $first$ to $last$ inclusive carries that many more passengers. Return the array of total passengers per flight.

Source: [LC 1109 · Corporate Flight Bookings](https://leetcode.com/problems/corporate-flight-bookings/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Each booking is a contiguous $+v$ over a range, and we only read the array once at the end — so never touch the range. Turn the value on at the first flight and off just after the last, then let one prefix sum spread it out.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Brute force.** For each booking loop $first \dots last$ and add: $O(n \cdot \text{bookings}) = 4\cdot10^{8}$ at the limits.
2. **Difference array.** With 1-based inclusive $[first, last]$, the half-open form is $[first-1, last)$ in 0-based indices: `d[first-1] += seats`, `d[last] -= seats`. Allocate $n+1$ cells so that $last = n$ still has somewhere to put its $-v$. Then prefix-sum the first $n$ cells.

**Invariant.** Cell $i$ of the rebuilt array equals the sum of `seats` over all bookings with $first \le i+1 \le last$, which is the definition of the answer.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Every cell of the range

::: {.form-next}
A booking says "these flights carry $s$ more", so touch those flights one at a time. Straightforward, always right, and $O(n \cdot b) = 4\cdot10^8$ at the limits — because the same cells are revisited by every booking that overlaps them.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def flight_bookings_brute(n, bookings):
    out = [0] * n
    for first, last, seats in bookings:
        for i in range(first - 1, last):
            out[i] += seats
    return out
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> corpFlightBookingsBrute(vector<vector<int>>& bookings, int n) {
    vector<long long> out(n, 0);
    for (auto& b : bookings)
        for (int i = b[0] - 1; i < b[1]; ++i)
            out[i] += b[2];
    vector<int> ans(out.begin(), out.end());
    return ans;
}
```
:::

#### Two writes per booking

::: {.form-next}
The array is read exactly once, at the end, so the range never has to be touched: turn the value **on** at `first - 1` and **off** just after `last`, two point writes, and let one prefix sum at the end spread each booking across the cells it covers. $O(1)$ per update again, and the allocate-$n{+}1$ rule is what lets a booking ending at $n$ write its $-s$ without going out of bounds.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("flight", "diff")
    assert str(final) == "[10, 55, 45, 25, 25]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-flight-bookings
def flight_bookings(n: int, bookings: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    d = [0] * (n + 1)                 # one spare cell for the last -v
    for first, last, seats in bookings:
        d[first - 1] += seats         # turn on
        d[last] -= seats              # turn off just after the range
    out, run = [], 0
    for i in range(n):
        run += d[i]
        out.append(run)
    return out


for _ in range(200):
    n = random.randint(1, 12)
    bookings = []
    for _ in range(6):
        first = random.randint(1, n)
        bookings.append([first, random.randint(first, n), random.randint(1, 9)])
    assert flight_bookings(n, bookings) == flight_bookings_brute(n, bookings)

assert flight_bookings(5, [[1, 2, 10], [2, 3, 20], [2, 5, 25]]) == [10, 55, 45, 25, 25]
assert flight_bookings(4, [[1, 4, 5], [1, 1, 2]]) == [7, 5, 5, 5]
assert flight_bookings(1, [[1, 1, 3]]) == [3]
print("flight_bookings OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> corpFlightBookings(vector<vector<int>>& bookings, int n) {
    vector<long long> d(n + 1, 0);
    for (auto& b : bookings) {
        d[b[0] - 1] += b[2];          // first is 1-based
        d[b[1]]     -= b[2];          // last is inclusive -> mark one after
    }
    vector<int> ans(n);
    long long run = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        run += d[i];
        ans[i] = (int)run;            // at most 2e4 * 1e4 = 2e8: fits int
    }
    return ans;
}
```
:::
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Every cell of the range** is $O(n \cdot b)$ time, $O(n)$ space. **Two writes per booking** is $O(n + b)$ time for $b$ bookings, and $O(n)$ space — and you can write the answer back into `d` to use no second array, the in-place prefix sum of @sec-arr-inplace.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- A booking with $last = n$: its $-v$ lands in `d[n]`, the spare cell. Size the array $n$ and this write is out of bounds — the classic crash for this pattern.
- A booking covering the whole array: two writes, regardless.
- Overlapping bookings: they simply accumulate in the same difference cells (the sum $10{+}20{+}25 = 55$ on flight 2 above).
- A judge that gives $0$-based inclusive ranges needs a different translation — decide the convention once, at the input boundary, and never mix.
:::
